A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Feedback Schrödinger Bridge Matching. All 25 pages of v1 and 29 pages of v3, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, support comparison; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original crowd-navigation, opinion-depolarization and image-translation experiments, including numerical comparisons in Tables 1–4 and appendix examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds image-coupling measurements, ChatGPT-based assessments and a guidance-function comparison.

M1.justification: The proposed nearest-keypoint guidance, Gaussian spline paths, alternating path/coupling optimization and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. The relation-preserving variant is an added comparison; guidance using multiple nearest keypoints remains future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate S-tunnel and V-neck navigation under the same initial-distribution scenarios, 100-dimensional opinion depolarization, and four FFHQ age/gender translation directions. Added metrics and guidance comparisons use this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix C and Figure 9 newly compare distance-preserving guidance with a relation-preserving variant inspired by Gu et al. (2022). The original benchmark comparator sets—GSBM, DeepGSB, DSBM and LOSBM in their respective experiments—are retained.

E3.justification: Image evaluation expands substantially beyond FID and visual examples: v3 adds LPIPS, normalized pixel L2 distance, SSIM and ChatGPT scoring. The latter evaluates 100 input/generated pairs per translation task on three criteria using a 0–5 scale, comparing FSBM with DSBM. These are additional evaluation procedures, without evidence that the original benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds a qualitative ablation testing whether relation-preserving versus distance-preserving guidance produces effective gradient fields. Existing distribution-shift tests and keypoint-count sensitivity are retained. The latter moves from v1 Figure 9 to v3 Figure 14, with Table 6 tabulating the existing study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added evaluations continue reporting point estimates; the initial-distribution standard deviations are experimental conditions, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical values, while Tables 5 and 7–11 substantially expand quantitative evidence about image-coupling preservation. For example, man-to-woman LPIPS is 0.44 for FSBM, 0.47 for DSBM and 0.70 for LOSBM. Results are mixed: DSBM exceeds FSBM on SSIM for woman-to-man (0.51 versus 0.47) and old-to-young (0.50 versus 0.46), although the ChatGPT scores favor FSBM throughout.

T1.justification: Proposition 3.5 and Appendix A.4 locally revise the Hamiltonian/duality argument, distinguishing the scalar multiplier from its gradient and explicitly invoking conjugate equality at the optimum. Section 3.2.2 removes the assertion that guidance terms are minimized only when G tends to zero. The main theorem conclusions remain unchanged; the added Appendix A.1 proof sketch principally explains existing reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a semi-supervised matching framework, a static-to-dynamic transport formulation, an entropic Lagrangian matching objective, and improved generalization and training efficiency using few aligned pairs.

C2.justification: v3 substantially sharpens applicability limits: Section 4.4 explains dependence on keypoint availability and quality, inadequate mode coverage, and resulting incorrect guidance or poor generalization. Appendix C also proposes a dynamic-versus-static explanation for the observed weakness of softmax-based relation-preserving guidance. v1 mainly discussed keypoint-count overfitting and deferred guidance comparisons.

D1.justification: v3 removes v1's RTX 4090 hardware disclosure, explicit 2,560-particle count and 2,048-image FID sample count. It adds pixel-distance normalization and ChatGPT assessment instructions, but omits the judge version and complete prompt. Shared architecture, optimizer and keypoint-construction details remain.

R1.justification: A dedicated Appendix C discussion substantially expands semi-supervised OT positioning beyond v1's introductory treatment. It distinguishes class-label regularization, Gromov–Wasserstein adaptation, anchor-based transport and paired-keypoint guidance, adding Courty et al. (2017), Yan et al. (2018) and Lin et al. (2021). Boyd and Vandenberghe is also added for the duality argument.

P1.justification: Method and training explanations receive focused rewrites, Appendix A gains a proof roadmap, and Section 4.4 becomes a limitations discussion. The keypoint-count discussion moves to Appendix C.1.1. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 replaces a schematic with time-resolved gradient fields, Figure 9 adds a guidance comparison, and Tables 5–11 expand the displays, including a numerical redisplay of the existing keypoint study. The original keypoint plot moves to appendix Figure 14, and several retained figures and tables are repositioned.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the previously largely qualitative coupling-quality claim more assessable, tests the guidance choice and explicitly identifies keypoint-coverage limitations. These provide a modest net quality gain. Benefits are limited by broad superiority language despite mixed L2/SSIM results, an underspecified ChatGPT assessment without uncertainty reporting, and removal of hardware and sample-count disclosures.
